title: sluis
_comment: Nothing is required here that the template already refuses to render without. The schema catches typos and wrong types; `required` in the template catches an unset value, with a sentence saying why it matters. Each component's `config` is generated into this file from the schema its binary validates against (`just config-schemas`); the rest is written in internal/config/schema/values.base.json.

nameOverride.description: Replaces the chart name in the `app.kubernetes.io/name` label and in the controllers' selector labels. An installation migrating from the access-issuer chart sets it to access-issuer so the Deployments' immutable selectors are unchanged.

fullnameOverride.description: Replaces the release's full name, the prefix of every object the chart renders and the value `config.release` must carry. An installation migrating from the access-issuer chart sets it to the old full name so no object is renamed.

perModule.description: Run each module from its own image (sluis-issuer, sluis-backup) beside image.repository, at the same tag, instead of the one multi-call image.

verifyOnly.description: PUBLIC keys the chart mounts from a ConfigMap (they are not secret), one file each at /var/run/access-issuer/verify-keys/<index>.pem, for `config.signingKey.verifyOnly[<index>].file`: published in the JWKS and never signed with. A private key is refused.

pem.description: A PEM public key, a certificate, or a JWK.

documents.description: The rendered documents of one installation (`sluisctl render`), each as the string the file holds. The chart puts them into their ConfigMaps unchanged and holds them to what it mounts; it does not rewrite them. Set both or neither. With them, `config`, `policy`, `exchange.clusters` and `exchange.aws.accounts` are not used.

clusters.description: Clusters whose workloads may exchange, each verified against the key set that cluster publishes. No secret in any row.

name.description: The estate's word for the cluster; what a workload matcher names.

jwksUri.description: Where its public keys are. Empty discovers it from the issuer.

aws.description: AWS accounts whose IAM roles may exchange their outbound-identity-federation token. Empty verifies none.

audience.description: The audience the role must request from STS. Empty means the issuer's own URL.

maxAge.description: Refuse a token whose iat is older, whatever its exp allows. Default 5m, at most 1h.

name.description: The estate's word for the account, for logs.

jwksUri.description: Where its public keys are. Empty means <issuer>/.well-known/jwks.json.

orgId.description: Require this AWS Organizations id in the token.

rootRedirect.description: Where a bare GET of the host root goes; empty serves 404.

awsIdentity.description: How the pod gets its AWS role. `pod-identity` (EKS Pod Identity) renders nothing: the association is made outside the chart. `irsa` annotates the account with `eks.amazonaws.com/role-arn: <awsRoleArn>`, which it requires.

catalogue.description: GitHub Apps declared as data, created and installed from the console. The service validates the whole catalogue again at start.

push.description: Copy this App's credential to a secret store with an External Secrets PushSecret: its three property keys only, to the store and path named here. Absent pushes nothing.

Copy the link App and one App per bound organisation to a secret store with an External Secrets PushSecret, for recovery: the whole Secret bundled under one remote key, because the key names inside it are not stable. Absent pushes nothing. deletionPolicy is deliberately not settable -- the case this exists for is the Secret going away.

secretManagers.description: Removed in v1.30.0 — the console's secret-store view was removed. Setting this key fails the render with a clear message. See CHANGELOG.md and docs/decisions/0002-mission-boundary-tokens-and-memberships.md.

audit.description: The projected service-account token this service and the controllers present to the audit installation. The installation itself (`audit.writer` and the rest) is the `config`'s.

audience.description: The audience of the projected token presented to the receiver.

adapters.description: What the chart mounts for the service's OpenBao connection (the `openbao` secrets adapter): the CA that signs OpenBao's certificate and the projected token the login presents. The address and how the service logs in are the `config`'s (`config.adapters.secrets`).

caBundle.description: PEM of the authorities that sign OpenBao's certificate. Rendered into a ConfigMap and mounted at /var/run/access-issuer/openbao-ca/ca.pem, which `config.adapters.secrets.settings.caFile` (the openbao Secrets adapter) must then be. Empty mounts nothing, and the system's authorities are trusted.

audience.description: The audience of a ServiceAccount token the chart projects at /var/run/openbao/token, for the `jwt` auth method (`config.adapters.secrets.settings.auth.tokenFile` must then be that path). Empty projects nothing: the `kubernetes` method reads the pod's own ServiceAccount token.

console.description: Where the console is mounted on the issuer's origin. The rest of what the console is configured with is the `config`'s.

mount.description: Where the console is mounted on this issuer's origin, e.g. /console. Empty serves no console.

directory.description: The corporate directories this service reads itself. The workspaces a deployment declares are the config's: `config.directory.workspaces`, each key file mounted with `secretMounts`.

push.description: Copy the credential of every connected workspace to a secret store with an External Secrets PushSecret, for recovery: the whole Secret bundled under one remote key, because the key names inside it are not stable. Absent pushes nothing. deletionPolicy is deliberately not settable -- the case this exists for is the Secret going away.

slackApps.description: Slack Apps declared as data, created and installed from the console. The service validates the whole catalogue again at start, and refuses an entry for a workspace the policy's slack.workspaces does not name.

workspace.description: A key of the policy's slack.workspaces.

push.description: Copy this App's bot token to a secret store with an External Secrets PushSecret: that one key only, to the store and path named here. Absent pushes nothing.

slackState.description: A recovery copy of the Slack state: see push.

push.description: Copy the credential of every connected Slack workspace, and the mirror of the records that say which workspaces and Slack Connect channels the console holds, to a secret store with an External Secrets PushSecret, for recovery: each whole Secret bundled under its own remote key (remoteKey for the credentials, recordsRemoteKey for the records), because the key names inside are not stable. Absent pushes nothing. deletionPolicy is deliberately not settable -- the case this exists for is the Secret going away.

secrets.description: The secrets the config names, each one key of a Secret projected as the file <config.secrets.root>/<name>.

name.description: The secret's name, as the config gives it: valkey/password.

backup.description: The backup module (docs/reference/sluis/backup.md): a CronJob that runs `sluis backup run`, an optional CronJob that prunes by the retention rule, and the document they read. Layout v5 only. Off by default. The restore Job (`restore`) reads the same document.

enabled.description: Render the backup CronJob, its ServiceAccount and the document's ConfigMap. Refused unless `config` names `backup.target` and layout v5.

schedule.description: Cron schedule of the backup run.

timeZone.description: IANA time zone of the schedule. Empty: the controller manager's.

suspend.description: Suspend the CronJobs without removing them.

concurrencyPolicy.description: The run takes a lease, so two at once would only wait on it: Forbid.

activeDeadlineSeconds.description: Stops a run after this many seconds. 0: no limit.

prune.description: A second CronJob that applies the retention rule (`sluis backup prune`).

enabled.description: Render it with the backup CronJob.

serviceAccount.description: The backup role's own account: it reads every module and writes the archive, so it is never the service's. Name empty: <release>-backup.

restore.description: The restore Job: for an administrator, off by default. Never a CronJob. It reads the document of `backup.config` and runs `sluis restore start`, with an account of its own, whose role may write every module's table.

enabled.description: Render one Job, named from `backupId`. Delete it before running the same restore again.

backupId.description: The backup to restore (`sluis backup list`). Exactly one of this and `resume`.

resume.description: Continue a restore that paused (`sluis restore start --resume`). No `backupId`.

confirm.description: The installation's name, `backup.config.instance`: a restore overwrites a live installation, and the Job is refused unless this says which one.

overwrite.description: Overwrite a destination that holds different data. Without it a non-empty destination is refused.

by.description: Who asked, for the audit record.

ttlSecondsAfterFinished.description: Remove the finished Job after this many seconds. 0: keep it.

activeDeadlineSeconds.description: Stops the Job after this many seconds. 0: no limit.

serviceAccount.description: The restore role's own account. Name empty: <release>-restore.

telemetry.description: The OpenTelemetry SDK environment on every pod of `renders: app` (ADR 0006). Nothing is rendered without `otlp.endpoint`.

legacyMetrics.description: Also publish the metrics under their old `access_issuer.*` and `access_roster.*` names (SLUIS_LEGACY_METRICS). On in v1.75; the old names and this key are removed in v1.76.

endpoint.description: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT: an http(s) URL naming the collector or gateway. Empty: nothing is exported and nothing is rendered.

extraEnv.description: Other OpenTelemetry SDK variables, name to value. Every name starts with OTEL_ and none is OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT (checked at render).

renders.description: What this release renders: `app`, the service and the controllers (the default); `alerts`, only the alert rules; `dashboards`, only the Grafana dashboard ConfigMaps. In the last two nothing else is rendered.

objectNamespace.description: Where the rule object goes. Empty: the release's namespace.

ruleLabels.description: Labels added to every rule, for Alertmanager routing, such as `k8s_cluster_name`.

interval.description: How often the ruler evaluates the group.

clusterLabel.description: The label that names the cluster on a store that holds several.

namespace.description: The namespace sluis runs in, whose series the rules read. Empty: the release's.

runbookBaseUrl.description: Where the runbook is; the alert's name, lower-cased, is the anchor. Empty renders no link.

for.description: How long the condition holds before the alert fires, as a duration.

labels.description: Labels added to this rule only.

signingKeyRotationStalled.description: The active signing key is older than `maxAgeSeconds`.

seatsShort.description: An organisation has fewer free seats than invitations.

folder.description: The Grafana folder, for a sidecar that reads the folder annotation.

sidecarLabel.description: The label Grafana's sidecar selects ConfigMaps by.

awsIdentity.description: How the pod gets its AWS role (as `serviceAccount.awsIdentity`).

secretEnv.description: Environment variables from a Secret's keys: the holders of the secrets the config names (`valkey.passwordEnv`, `oauthClient.secretEnv`, `adminPasswordEnv`). A secret is never in `config`.

name.description: The variable, as the config names it.

optional.description: Start without it when the Secret or the key is absent.

secretMounts.description: Secrets mounted read-only as directories, for a file the config names by path (`oauthClient.idFile`, `oauthClient.secretFile`). Each key is a file.
